title: The Cell System: a coordinate system for the odd sieve — what it proves, what it measures, and where it stops
description:
Twelve papers, one overview and twenty-nine verification scripts on the elementary sieve of the odd numbers, developed as a coordinate system of lines and cells.

Papers 1 to 4 build the coordinates and the transport laws: an exact histogram for the increments of floor(2j²/n) with no error term, the line/cell coordinate system, the exact inheritance law on a full sieve cycle, and what survives when that law is evaluated on a short interval. Papers 5 to 8 are the construction and what it decides about twin pairs: the three-letter gap alphabet, the six exception positions of the twin criterion, clocks and the capacity of a single line, and the belts between consecutive prime squares. Papers 9 to 11 derive the point at which the construction stops, from inside it rather than by quoting it: the depth cut, the unique-owner theorem, the exact twin count T = C − R + S with no error term and the parity identity 2(R − C) = Σ(−1)Ω; then why no ordinary sieve crosses it; then four tests of the framework against problems whose answers are known independently; and finally what an external ingredient would have to supply, with every route already tried recorded and closed.

The framework reproduces Buchstab's decomposition, the Hardy–Littlewood singular series and the exact factor-of-two loss I(s) = 2f1(s) without importing them, and then halts exactly where the field halts. (The sifting limits are quoted from the literature, not derived here.) Paper 1 is independent of the rest and concerns no prime numbers.

Statements that are only measured are labelled as such and listed together; results produced and then retracted during the work are kept rather than deleted. No progress toward the twin-prime conjecture is claimed, and no new bound. Priority is not claimed for any result.

Release 1.0.0 of this record. It supersedes an earlier archived record of the same work, and it splits the earlier seven-document set into eleven parts and an overview, adds a twelfth, renumbers every result per paper, and carries the corrections of three independent review passes over that text. The L² experiment of Paper 4 was measuring a deterministic bookkeeping term created by a wrong normalisation, and also named the wrong quantity: the section is rewritten, the growth it reported is withdrawn, and the nested deviations the telescoping identity actually needs are measured beside the raw ones. A corollary of Paper 2 was false for half of the primes, through a phase convention that differed between the text and the script that verifies it. The Fréchet floor of Paper 9 holds only when the two composite rates sum above one, which at the rates measured they do not, so the vanishing state needs the marginals to move and not the correlation alone. A conclusion of Paper 10 — that every weighted first-moment argument assumes its conclusion — was a mistake in logic and is withdrawn: the route is open and unequipped, not closed. The per-bin generating function of Paper 3 needed two markers per bin to carry the joint law it claimed, and Richert's weight is restated with the multiplicity its detection mechanism requires. A theorem of Paper 10 is restricted to the belt its proof and its script both use. Alongside these, the identity H = 2 + W underlying the window count is now proved where it is first used, the definitions Theorem 3 of Paper 4 depends on are moved into that paper, and a cut in Paper 11 that failed its own hypothesis as written is restated in the form its proof gives. Twenty-nine verification scripts regenerate every number printed, each exiting non-zero when the claim it supports fails; a new coverage table records for each one the definition it computes rather than only the section it covers; and a further script emits the certificate behind the exception budget of Paper 6 — the 28 maximal configurations, every prime that eliminates each of the 27, and an admissible residue for the survivor at every prime — which was asserted in the text and produced by nothing, and whose writing corrected two of the numbers in that passage.
